A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PianoMotion10M and the same hand-motion generation benchmark. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations in Table 3, denoising-step ablations in Table 4 and generated-motion examples in Figure 4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds qualitative failure examples for excessively fast music in Figure A3.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the position predictor, position-conditioned diffusion gesture generator, audio encoders, losses and two-stage training procedure. The revised per-hand tensor notation does not establish an architectural or procedural change.

E1.justification: The same PianoMotion10M corpus and audio-to-hand-motion task remain. Appendix D and Figure A3 add a qualitative evaluation scenario involving excessively fast music. Multi-hand and non-human audio are mentioned as limitations without separate demonstrated evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains EmoTalk, LivelySpeaker and the same proposed-model configurations. The additional datasets surveyed in Table 1 and newly cited transcription methods are not additional competitors evaluated against the hand-motion generator.

E3.justification: v2's new Equation (6) specifies squared L2 distance for PD, whereas v1 describes L2 distance. This changes the written metric specification, although v2 retains the L2 prose and identical scores, so an implementation change or rerun is not established. Split counts, model configurations and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds qualitative error analysis illustrating incorrect hand transitions under excessively fast music in Figure A3. The existing denoising-step ablation in Table 4 and architecture comparisons are retained without changed results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, variability estimates or significance tests for the benchmark results.

E6.justification: Figure A3 adds concrete qualitative failure outputs. All numerical entries in Tables 3 and 4 are unchanged after matching Table 3's reversed left/right-hand column groups; for example, the large HuBERT/Transformer model retains FID 3.281.

T1.justification: The squared-L2 expression for PD in v2 Equation (6) is not equivalent to v1's L2-distance description, creating a limited formal-definition discrepancy. The added FID and FGD formulas otherwise explain existing metrics; the diffusion mathematics and assumptions are retained, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the 116-hour dataset with approximately 10 million annotated poses, the evaluation benchmark and the two-component generation baseline. The claimed instructional purpose and dataset novelty remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly discusses subject imbalance and out-of-distribution failures involving rapid, multi-hand or non-human performances, while retaining keyboard-alignment and recording-tone limitations. Section 5.1 also introduces the interpretation of FGD as global/long-term alignment and WGD as localized/short-term similarity.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents original-video-level splitting, creator-provided MIDI, MIDI correction thresholds and Savitzky-Golay order 3/window 11. Appendix E supplies a creator-permission account. The abstract changes the access destination from the project page to a repository, but Appendix G's third-party tool/baseline URLs and licenses are removed. These disclosures do not establish regenerated data.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a substantial piano-hand-specific review, including earlier motion synthesis, posture assessment and piano datasets. Table 1 adds CMU Panoptic and four piano-hand datasets, with availability comparisons supporting a stronger emphasis on open access. Additional transcription references further broaden the positioning beyond the earlier general motion discussion.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Changes include expanded metric explanations, a rewritten ethics discussion, acknowledgments, removal of Appendix G, author/affiliation edits and author-year citation formatting. This is localized revision rather than wholesale narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 expands Table 1 with dataset rows and year/availability columns, aggregates seven subjects into 'Others' in Table 2, reverses Table 3's hand groups and adds Figure A3. Existing figures largely retain their content, including Figures 5/6 becoming A1/A2, within the revised ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through more relevant prior-work comparisons, clearer data-preparation and consent documentation, and illustrated failure conditions. These gains are partly offset by removal of Appendix G's access/license details and the new PD equation/prose inconsistency. The evidence supports a limited net improvement around the retained method and benchmark.
